einzeiler: Nova and Pip study a soccer game and discover that fair does not always mean equal.
kurzfassung: Nova and Pip observe children playing soccer on an Earth sports field and wonder about the rules and fairness. They are confused why one child has to sit on the bench without playing time while others run around. Ultimately, they learn from their agent that fairness can mean everyone gets what they need rather than an equal amount.
stichpunkte: Nova and Pip trade computer time before detecting a new mission on an Earth sports field.
They observe children kicking a round object they call an orb ball in a game identified as soccer or football.
The players are divided into red and yellow shirts, kicking the ball back and forth until a goal is scored.
Pip expresses concern for a child sitting on the bench who gets zero seconds of playing time.
A player with a different role catches the ball with her hands to guard the net.
The benched child finally enters the field with fresh legs, running faster than the tired players.
Pip secretly kicks the left-behind orb ball and celebrates making contact with a real Earth object.
The agent confirms that a situation can be fair even when it is not equal, helping Pip understand team roles.

kapitel.titel: The Benched Player and Fresh Legs

clips.text: Two companions argue over screen time distribution before agreeing that access to the device ought to be shared fairly.
Data analysis indicates a high likelihood that the sport is called football or soccer based on kicking actions.
Concern arises regarding a participant forced to remain seated on the bench while everyone else gets to play.

Pip and Nova arrive at a school sports field and quickly become fascinated by humans kicking an “orb-ball” into a net. But when one child spends most of the game sitting on the bench, Pip starts wondering: How is that fair?
As the game unfolds, they discover that different players can have different roles, different amounts of playing time, and still all matter to the team.

Along the way, they learn that fair doesn’t always mean equal. Sometimes, fair means everyone gets what they need.
